checks.note: Citation re-sourced 2026-09-21: the official observatory page no longer renders the array figures (QA review §7.6); the detector paper abstract states them verbatim.
checks.quote: The Auger design features an array of 1660 water-Cherenkov particle detector stations spread over 3000 km² overlooked by 24 air fluorescence telescopes.

geometry.note: Confidence 'derived': the vertices are real surveyed station positions, but the hull itself is this session's computation, not a published boundary.

method: Convex hull (planar monotone-chain algorithm) of the 1640 stations flagged sd1500=1 in the Observatory's own public sdMap.csv (Auger Open Data, Zenodo record 10488964; 1690 rows total, 1618 sd1500-only + 22 dual-flagged sd1500/sd750). Station UTM zone 19S northing/easting converted to WGS84 lat/lon by the standard Snyder inverse-UTM series (this session's own computation of a public official coordinate list, not itself a claim from the source). A convex hull necessarily overestimates the true, non-convex array footprint (computed area 3160.6 km^2 vs. the collaboration's own round '3000 km2' figure, +5.35%, still within the 8% check tolerance below); accuracy_m 50 covers this plus the dataset's own unstated per-station GPS precision. Includes every station ever flagged sd1500 in the release regardless of its own start/stop activity window, i.e. the maximal historical footprint, not a snapshot of only currently active stations (some of the 1660 nominal stations are decommissioned/replaced; 1640 rows carried the flag in this release).
name: Pierre Auger Observatory surface-detector array (1500 m spacing), convex hull
notes: This is a convex hull, not the true (slightly concave/irregular) instrumented boundary; see method for the resulting +5.35% area overestimate against the collaboration's own '3000 km2' figure, still inside the 8% check tolerance used here.

summary.plain: The outer boundary of the Pierre Auger Observatory's main array of water-tank detectors, drawn by connecting the outermost of the array's own surveyed station positions.
